app.name: Gmail (Google Gmail API via a Google Cloud OAuth client)

verdict.summary: You can create a Google Cloud OAuth client and connect your own Gmail account in minutes, but in Testing mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days and the number of users is capped. Going public with restricted Gmail scopes such as https://mail.google.com/ (Composio's default) requires brand verification, restricted-scope verification and an annual paid CASA security assessment. That process takes weeks.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for Testing mode; 1-3 days of active work for verification (domain, privacy policy, demo video, justifications), plus security assessment work
verdict.approval_wait: Sensitive scopes: 3-5 business days. Restricted scopes (e.g. https://mail.google.com/, gmail.readonly, gmail.modify): several weeks (about 6 weeks reported), plus a third-party CASA assessment

gates.name: Testing mode (your own account)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Google account (added as a test user) through your own OAuth client with any scopes, including restricted Gmail scopes, without verification.
limits: The consent screen shows a tester warning
Refresh tokens expire after 7 days for External apps in Testing, unless the app requests only name, email and profile
Only listed test accounts can authorize

gates.name: Testing mode with test users
gates.unlocks: Google accounts you add to the test-user list can connect without any Google review.
limits: A user cap applies. Google states 100 new users in total for apps that show the unverified-app screen
7-day refresh token lifetime, so users must reconnect weekly
You must keep the test-user list up to date yourself

gates.name: In production and verified (brand + sensitive/restricted scope verification)
gates.unlocks: Any Google account can connect with no warning screen and no user cap.
limits: Restricted-scope apps that access data through a server must pass a security assessment by a Google-approved third party every year
Reverification and reassessment are due at least every 12 months after the Letter of Assessment date
A compliant brand verification result is valid for only 7 days, so you must publish within that window
Google may revoke tokens that contain these scopes if the approval lapses
gates.time_to_reach: About 3-5 business days if you use sensitive scopes only. Several weeks (about 6 reported) plus a CASA security assessment if you use restricted scopes such as https://mail.google.com/

steps.title: Sign in and create Google Cloud projects
steps.detail: Sign in to the Google Cloud Console with the Google account that will own the app. Create the project inside a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization if you have one, so the project isn't orphaned if its owner leaves. Google's policies require separate projects for each deployment tier, such as development and production.
gotchas: The Console requires sign-in. Use an organization account, not a personal account, for the production project.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen (branding and audience)
steps.detail: In the project's OAuth consent screen settings, set User type to External and leave the publishing status as Testing. Enter the app name, support email, home page, privacy policy link and authorized domains. The authorized domains must include the domain of every redirect URI and JavaScript origin on your Web application client, which includes Composio's callback domain if you use it.
gotchas: The privacy policy must be on the same domain as the home page before brand verification can pass.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes and declare them on the Data Access page
steps.detail: List the Gmail actions your agent actually uses and map each one to the narrowest scope. Only use https://mail.google.com/ if you need IMAP/SMTP or full access. Add exactly those scopes on the consent screen's Data Access page, where Google shows whether each one is non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted. The scopes you declare must match the scopes your app (and your Composio auth config) requests.
gotchas: Composio's default Gmail scope set includes https://mail.google.com/, which is restricted. Trim it if you don't need full access.
Sources disagree on whether gmail.send is restricted. Check what the Data Access page shows.

steps.title: Add test users
steps.detail: Under the consent screen's audience/test users section, add your own Google account and each tester's account. Only these accounts can authorize while the app is in Testing.
gotchas: Testers see a warning screen, and their refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.detail: On the Clients/Credentials page, create an OAuth client ID with application type 'Web application'. Under Authorized redirect URIs, paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config. Copy the client ID and client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The scheme, case and trailing slash must match exactly, or Google rejects the request with a redirect mismatch.

steps.title: Connect your own account through Composio and test
steps.detail: Enter the client ID, client secret and chosen scopes in a Composio Gmail auth config, then run an authorization with a test account. Confirm that a refresh token comes back: offline access is required, and Google returns a refresh token only on the first authorization. Also confirm that the state value is validated.
gotchas: If you re-run consent without prompt=consent, you may not get a new refresh token.

steps.title: Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console
steps.detail: Verify every authorized domain (home page, privacy policy and redirect domains you control) in Google Search Console, using an account that is an Owner or Editor on the Cloud project.
gotchas: You can't verify a domain you don't own. Check how Composio's callback domain is handled in brand verification; this is an open question.

steps.title: Publish a home page, privacy policy and scope justifications
steps.detail: Draft and publish a public home page on your verified domain that links to your terms and privacy policy. Host the privacy policy on the same domain and say how Gmail data is used. Write a justification for each sensitive or restricted scope that explains why a narrower scope won't work.

steps.title: Run brand verification and publish to production
steps.detail: Submit the branding for verification. If the automated checks can't decide, a manual review usually takes 2-3 business days. Once the result is compliant, set the publishing status to In production within 7 days. Google requires a published branding status before you can request data-access verification.
gotchas: A compliant result expires after 7 days. If you publish late, you have to verify again.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record a video that shows the full OAuth grant flow and each sensitive and restricted scope being used in your app. Upload it to YouTube with Visibility set to Unlisted.

steps.title: Submit the data-access (scope) verification request
steps.detail: In the Data Access/verification section, submit your scopes with their justifications and the video link. Select your permitted application type from the 'What features will you use?' list.

steps.title: Wait for Google's review and complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Sensitive-scope review typically takes 3-5 business days. Restricted-scope review can take several weeks; one third-party table cites about 6 weeks. For restricted scopes, you must also pass a CASA security assessment with a Google-approved lab. Google charges no fee, but the labs set their own prices; one third-party list gives $540-$1,800 for Tier 2.
steps.est_time: 3-5 business days (sensitive); several weeks or more (restricted)
gotchas: A community report says Tier 2 self-scan is no longer available, so plan to use an approved lab.

steps.title: Plan annual reverification and keep the client active
steps.detail: Restricted-scope apps must be reverified and reassessed at least every 12 months after the Letter of Assessment date. Google may delete OAuth clients that have been inactive for at least 6 months.

requirements.item: Publicly accessible home page on a verified domain you own, linking to terms and privacy policy
requirements.detail: Required for every production OAuth app.

requirements.item: Privacy policy on the same domain as the home page, linked from the consent screen
Domain ownership verified in Google Search Console
requirements.detail: Done by an Owner or Editor of the Cloud project, for each authorized domain.

requirements.item: Authorized domains include the domains of the redirect URIs and JavaScript origins
requirements.detail: Applies to every Web application OAuth client in the project.
Required before you can request sensitive/restricted scope verification. A compliant result is valid for 7 days.
Shows the grant flow and each sensitive or restricted scope in use.
Explain why narrower scopes are not enough, e.g. why a send-only app would need full mail access.
Done by a Google-approved third-party lab, with reassessment every 12 months.
You must maintain the list of Google accounts allowed to use the app in Testing.

scopes.effect: Full mailbox access, also needed for IMAP/SMTP. Requires restricted-scope verification and a CASA assessment. Included in Composio's default scope set.

scopes.scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing
scopes.effect: A third-party analysis lists these as restricted, so expect restricted-scope verification and CASA. Confirm on the Data Access page.
Sources disagree on the classification. If it is not restricted, a send-only agent may avoid CASA. Check the Data Access page.
If you request only name, email and profile, Testing-mode refresh tokens don't expire after 7 days.
Part of Composio's default set, but no tier was confirmed in the research. Drop them if unused, because every declared sensitive scope adds to review.

blockers.symptom: Users must reconnect Gmail every 7 days (invalid_grant on refresh)
blockers.cause: External apps in Testing get refresh tokens that expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Publish the app to In production. If it uses sensitive or restricted scopes, complete verification.

blockers.symptom: 'Google hasn't verified this app' screen, and new users are blocked after a cap
blockers.cause: The app uses sensitive or restricted scopes without approval. Google caps it at 100 new users in total.
blockers.fix: Submit for verification. Don't add new sensitive or restricted scopes before they are approved.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI in the request doesn't exactly match one on the client (scheme, case or trailing slash).
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into Authorized redirect URIs.

blockers.symptom: invalid_client: The OAuth client was not found
blockers.fix: Copy the client ID again from the Credentials page. Clients that have been inactive for 6 months or more may be deleted; they can be restored within 30 days.

blockers.symptom: No refresh_token in the token response
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens are returned only on the first authorization, and only with access_type=offline.
blockers.fix: Request access_type=offline. Use prompt=consent to re-prompt and get a new refresh token.

blockers.cause: The Workspace admin has blocked your client from sensitive or restricted scopes.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer's Workspace admin to allow your OAuth client.

blockers.symptom: Tokens suddenly revoked after previously working
blockers.cause: Restricted or sensitive scope approval lapsed (e.g. a missed annual reassessment), or the user revoked access.
blockers.fix: Keep reverification current every 12 months, and handle refresh failures by asking the user to reconnect.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Gmail OAuth to build and demo without your own Google app. Use your own Google Cloud client when you need your own branding on the consent screen or your own scope set. If you copy Composio's default scopes, the restricted https://mail.google.com/ scope puts you into restricted-scope verification and annual CASA. Trim to the narrowest scopes you need first. For a few testers, your own client in Testing mode works immediately, but refresh tokens expire after 7 days. The research did not confirm whether Composio's shared app is verified for these scopes.

open_questions: Google's official per-scope sensitive/restricted list for Gmail wasn't retrieved. Third-party sources disagree on gmail.send, so confirm each tier on the Cloud Console Data Access page.
The findings don't cover the step of enabling the Gmail API in the Cloud project's API Library; confirm this during setup.
Google's own CASA timeline and 2026 pricing weren't confirmed on an official page; the cost and turnaround figures come from third-party sites.
It is unknown whether Composio's shared Google OAuth app is verified for the restricted scopes it requests, and what limits apply to managed Gmail auth.
It is unclear how brand verification treats a Composio-owned callback domain listed under Authorized domains, since you can't verify ownership of it in Search Console.
PKCE for the server-side web flow wasn't confirmed in the web-server guide, though Google's discovery document advertises S256.
The Console steps are based on Google's documentation, not a live Console view (the probe hit a sign-in wall), so menu labels may differ slightly.
